{{Short description|American physicist}}
{{other people|Jeff Schmidt}}

'''Jeff Schmidt''' is a [[physicist]] who wrote the 2000 book ''Disciplined Minds'', a critique of the socialization and training of professionals.<ref>{{cite book| authorlink=Jeff Schmidt (writer)| year=2000| title=Disciplined Minds: A Critical Look at Salaried Professionals and the Soul-Battering System that Shapes Their Lives| publisher=Rowman & Littlefield| isbn=978-0-8476-9364-1| author=Jeff Schmidt.| url-access=registration| url=https://archive.org/details/disciplinedminds00schm}}</ref>

==Termination of employment controversy==
Schmidt was [[Termination of employment|fired]] from his job of 19&nbsp;years as an associate editor for ''[[Physics Today]]'', the magazine of the [[American Institute of Physics]] (AIP), on allegations that he wrote the book on his employer's time.<ref>{{cite journal| author=Sharlet, Jeff |author2=Rurak, Jennifer K. |title=''Physics Today'' Fires Author of Book on 'Soul-Battering System' of the Workplace| journal= The Chronicle of Higher Education |date= 9 June 2000 |url= http://chronicle.com/weekly/v46/i40/40a02401.htm}}</ref> The book starts: "This book was stolen. Written in part on stolen time, that is." Schmidt contended, however, that he was fired for "protesting discriminatory hiring practices" at AIP, and that the "stolen time" quotation was an exaggerated allusion to [[counterculture]] icon [[Abbie Hoffman]], who wrote ''[[Steal This Book]]''. He added that "writing this radical book during break time in the office felt like stealing time because the ideas that I was expressing seemed so out of place with the corporate-type [[Organizational culture|atmosphere]] of the office."<ref name=highered /> Schmidt's firing led to a public campaign, with 750&nbsp;physicists and academics, including [[Noam Chomsky]], signing a letter supporting Schmidt.<ref name=highered>{{cite news|last=Monastersky|first=Richard|title=Physics Editor Wins Settlement in Case Over Discrimination|url=http://chronicle.com/article/Physics-Editor-Wins-Settlement/5838|accessdate=4 October 2012|newspaper=The Chronicle of Higher Education|date=24 March 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author= Rurak, Jennifer K.| title= Physicists Unite in Defense of Time-Pilfering Editor | journal= The Chronicle of Higher Education | date= 5 April 2002 | url=http://chronicle.com/weekly/v48/i30/30a01201.htm}}</ref>

==Legal settlement==
The public campaign in turn led to a legal case, carried by [[Washington Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights and Urban Affairs|Washington Lawyers Committee for Civil Rights and Urban Affairs]], a law firm specializing in [[Civil liberties in the United States|civil liberties]], that produced an undisclosed financial [[Settlement (litigation)|settlement]] for Schmidt, including anti-discrimination policy changes at AIP.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Cho, Adrian|title=Physics Institute Settles Suit, Takes Steps to Increase Diversity| journal=Science | volume=311 | date=31 Mar 2006| url=http://www.sciencemag.org/cgi/content/full/311/5769/1848b| pages=1848|  doi=10.1126/science.311.5769.1848b |pmid=16574830 |issue=5769|s2cid=25586656 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> even though AIP did not admit any wrongdoing, it admitted that Schmidt "consistently received positive [[Performance appraisal|job reviews]]" and rehired Schmidt, who immediately [[Resignation|resign]]ed.<ref name=highered />
